 :JUDGMENT:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioners against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.50,00,000/ for the death of Sanjay Kumar S/o Shivanna in a Road Traffic accident.

The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 21.11.2022 at about 6.30 p.m., when the son of the Petitioner No.1 and 2 by name Sanjay Kumar was proceeding by riding his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA 06EV4404 from Kunigal side towards Yadiyuru side and at that time, one Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA19AD5400 which was driven by its driver came from Kunigal side towards Yadiyur side in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life and dashed against the Sanjay Kumar's motorcycle.
Due to the said impact, Sanjay Kumar has fell down and sustained fatal injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
Thereafter, Postmortem was conducted at Government hospital, Kunigal and then body was handed over to the Petitioners.
Petitioners had spent about Rs.90,000/ towards transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.
3. Prior to the date of accident, the deceased was hale and SCCH 15 4 MVC No.1899/2023 healthy and he was doing labour work and was earning Rs.20,000/ per month.
The Petitioners entirely depending upon the income of the deceased.
The Respondent No.1 is the owner and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA19AD5400.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
4. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, the Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.
The Respondent No.2 had appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed its Written statement to the main Petition.

The Respondent No.1 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending lorry.

Further it contended that, accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the Chikkayashodamma vs Prajeeth Sharon D Souza on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168845024/
2 deceased who being SCCH 15 5 MVC No.1899/2023 rider of the motorcycle rode the same in a rash and negligent manner without wearing helmet and without following traffic rules and regulations and caused the accident.

To rebut the SCCH 15 11 MVC No.1899/2023 evidence of PW.1, the Respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any evidence.
Hence, they failed to substantiate their Objection Statement contentions.
The Respondent No.2 had taken contention that on the alleged date, the deceased did not wear helmet.
Hence, there is a contributory negligence on the part of the deceased towards the said accident.

But,
the Ex.P2 Complaint recitals clearly shows that the deceased Sanjay Kumar was proceeding in his motorcycle by wearing helmet.
Moreover, the Chargesheet does not show that the deceased died not wear the helmet on the alleged date.
Hence, the contention taken by the Respondent No.2 did not prove.

Under such circumstances,
this Tribunal is of the opinion that the PW.1 has proved the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA19AD5400 by its driver and in the said accident her son Sanjay Kumar was succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, I answer

It is averred in the Petition that the Petitioner No.1 is the mother of the deceased,
Petitioner No.2 is the father of the deceased and Petitioner No.3 is the younger sister of the deceased Sanjay Kumar.
To prove their relationship with the deceased, PW.1 has produced Aadhaar cards of the deceased and Petitioners at Ex.P.8 to Ex.P.13.
Upon going through the same, it clearly shows the relationship of the deceased Sanjay Kumar with the Petitioners.
Hence, the Petitioners have proved that they are the legal heirs of the deceased Sanjay Kumar 15.
Further, the Petitioners have stated the age of the deceased Sanjay Kumar was 25 years at the time of the accident.

In this regard Petitioners have produced Ex.P13 i.e.,
Aadhaar card of the deceased which shows the date of birth of the deceased was 21.01.1997.
The accident took place on SCCH 15 13 MVC No.1899/2023 21.11.2022.
Hence, the age of the deceased was Sanjay Kumar was 26 years at the time of accident and the same to be taken for the purpose of Assessment.
16. In the petition, the Petitioners have stated that the deceased Sanjay Kumar was doing labour work and was earning Rs.20,000/.
But, PW.1 has not produced any document in this regard.
Therefore, in the absence of income proof, the notional income to be taken at Rs.15,500/ per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
17. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:
18.
The deceased has left behind his father, mother and SCCH 15 14 MVC No.1899/2023 younger sister.
Hence, the Petitioners are considered as dependents.

At this juncture, I would like to go through principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has pleased to observed that : "Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 15,000/, loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/ and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/".

Thus, totally the Petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.23,38,400/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.

24. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA19AD5400.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
There is no dispute about the validity of the policy at the time accident.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "in the SCCH 15 21 MVC No.1899/2023 Affirmative" and Issue No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".
25. Issue No.4:
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for compensation of Rs.23,38,400/ along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.23,38,400/ along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly SCCH 15 22 MVC No.1899/2023 and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.2 being the Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 45% each to the Petitioner No.1 and 2.
2) 10% to the Petitioner No.3.

After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 and 2, 50% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Chikkayashodamma vs Prajeeth Sharon D Souza on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168845024/

ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.23,38,400/ along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly SCCH 15 22 MVC No.1899/2023 and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.

9 Petitioner No.1 and 2 by way of Epayment and after their proper identification and the remaining 50% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 and 2 in any SCCH 15 23 MVC No.1899/2023 Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of their choice.
The entire amount awarded to the share of the Petitioner No.3 shall be released to her by way of E payment and after her proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/.
 Draw Award accordingly.
